questions.stem:
While reviewing a Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed (RACI) matrix, an auditor finds that the chief information security officer (CISO), the compliance officer, and the information technology (IT) manager are all assigned the same role for regulatory audits. This has led to conflicting decisions.

Which RACI role should be limited to one person for the task?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Accountable

In a Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed (RACI) matrix, the Accountable role holds final ownership of a task and the authority to decide. Each task should have exactly one accountable person so responsibility is not split. When several people share that role, decisions can conflict, as they did here.

The Responsible role is assigned to the person or group who executes the task. More than one person, such as the security and information technology (IT) teams, can share this role.

The Consulted role is assigned to subject matter experts or stakeholders who provide input before a decision is made. Several people can be consulted on a single task.

The Informed role is assigned to those who are kept up to date on progress or outcomes without contributing directly. Executive leadership and board members are commonly informed, and many people can hold this role.

questions.stem: A software development company wants to test its code in an environment where it cannot make changes to the operating system or other files outside of its restricted area. Which type of solution should they use for this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Sandboxing

Sandboxing is a technique for limiting the ability of code to affect the rest of the system. This can be useful for testing an application in development or for running untrusted applications.

Code signing is used to verify an application's author and that the code has not changed in transit.

Virtualization is a broader concept that doesn't specifically disallow changes to the guest OS.

Clustering is used for improved performance and fault tolerance.

questions.stem: Which answer option BEST describes RTO?

options.text: It is a metric used to determine the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
It is a metric that defines the maximum allowable amount of time that a system can be unavailable after a disruption before it causes significant damage to the organization
It is an agreement that specifies the extent to which a service or system must be recovered and operational after a disruption
It is an agreement between a service provider and a customer that defines the standards and expectations for the delivery of a service

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It is a metric that defines the maximum allowable amount of time that a system can be unavailable after a disruption before it causes significant damage to the organization

The Recovery Time Objective (RTO) measures how quickly a system must be restored after a disruption to avoid unacceptable consequences for the organization. For example, if your RTO is two hours, your disaster recovery plan must ensure that the system is back online within two hours of an outage.

The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is a metric that defines the maximum allowable amount of data loss that is acceptable from an incident and determines the frequency of backups.

A Recovery Service Level (RSL) is an agreement that specifies the extent to which a service or system must be recovered and operational after a disruption.

A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is an agreement between a service provider and a customer that defines the standards and expectations for the delivery of a service.

questions.stem: Ransomware that exploited a Server Message Block (SMB) vulnerability spread rapidly between servers within a company's data center after infecting a single host. Which control BEST restricts this east-west movement in the future?

options.text: A second firewall at the internet perimeter
A host-based intrusion detection system on each server

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Microsegmentation

Once attackers control one system, they typically spread to others, moving east-west across the network by taking advantage of weak segmentation or stolen credentials. In the WannaCry outbreak, the EternalBlue exploit for a Server Message Block (SMB) flaw let the malware jump from system to system. Microsegmentation limits east-west traffic so this kind of unauthorized lateral movement is blocked.

A host-based intrusion detection system can detect suspicious activity on each server. It alerts on the spread rather than restricting traffic between servers.

A second perimeter firewall controls north-south traffic entering and leaving the network. The ransomware spread east-west between servers inside the data center.

Signature-based updates help detect known malware. They do not restrict network paths between servers, and new variants may not match existing signatures.

Choose THREE.

options.text: Training employees for social engineering attacks

Meeting stakeholder needs aligns IT governance with business goals. Applying a single integrated framework ensures a consistent approach to IT governance and management. Separating governance from management enhances organizational efficiency.

COBIT focuses on IT governance rather than specific cybersecurity training programs such as training employees for social engineering attacks.

questions.stem:
A legal team questions the authenticity of a video submitted as evidence. A forensic analyst needs to review its codec information, encoding parameters, and timestamps to look for signs of tampering.

Which tool should the analyst use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: MediaInfo

Audio and video metadata analysis reviews information stored inside media files, such as the codec, encoding settings, timestamps, creation details, and the software used to edit the file. It helps confirm whether a file is authentic or has been altered. MediaInfo shows the technical details of audio and video files, including codecs, encoding parameters, and timestamps.

JPEGsnoop analyzes image metadata and compression signatures to detect manipulation of images. It is not designed for video files.

Autopsy/The Sleuth Kit analyzes filesystem metadata, reconstructs timelines, and tracks file interactions. It does not inspect the codec and encoding details inside a video file.

MxToolbox analyzes email headers to identify sending Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and routing paths. It does not analyze multimedia files.

questions.stem:
Which of the following cloud controls represent a proactive strategy?

Choose TWO.

options.text: An administrator implements a control to determine if any data contains personally identifiable information that must be protected
An administrator analyzes AWS CloudTrail logs for unusual activity
An administrator uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to give a user a role that has read-only access to certain company documents
An administrator uses Terraform with guardrails to block the creation of public S3 buckets
An administrator sets up an Azure Key Vault to rotate secrets regularly

questions.explanation:
Proactive cloud security controls are a type of preventive control that shift left, or, in other words, involves embedding security checks earlier in the development lifecycle, such as through Infrastructure as Code (IaC) templates. Blocking the creation of non-compliant S3 buckets with Terraform is proactive because it blocks insecure resources from being provisioned in the first place. Automatically rotating secrets reduces the attack window and is a preventive control to limit exposure if credentials are leaked. 

Using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to give a user a role is a preventive control but is not considered proactive because it is not dynamic or implemented with IaC.

Analyzing AWS CloudTrail logs for unusual activity is a detective control.

Determining if any data contains personally identifiable information is also a detective control.

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to the amount or percentage of time a system is accessible and functional?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Availability

Availability is the amount of time or percentage of the time a computer system is available for use. During the determination of the availability of a system, the following terms are typically used:

Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD)
Mean Time To Repair (MTTR)
Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)

Reliability is a system's consistency in performing correctly without failure.

Redundancy is a strategy for improving availability by having multiple systems.

Integrity involves ensuring that data is accurate and unaltered.

questions.stem:
Which conditions can lead to a situation where AI has excessive agency?

Choose THREE.
questions.explanation:
AI systems that have excessive agency could take impactful actions without sufficient oversight, which creates risks related to safety, ethics, and control issues. An AI system that is granted too many permissions such as root-level access to systems could perform powerful actions unchecked. AI systems with high autonomy are allowed to make decisions and act without human intervention, which could lead to unsafe behaviors. AI systems with broad capabilities, such as managing security systems or making business decisions, could lead to situations where AI takes too much control.

High processing power increases the speed of computations but does not inherently give the AI more decision-making power or control over systems. 

Large storage may raise privacy concerns but does not directly increase agency.

Which of the following accurately describe SD- WAN?

Choose TWO.

options.text: SD-WAN only operates in Layer 2 of the OSI model
It allows networks to route traffic based on application needs rather than physical topologies
SD-WAN eliminates the need for any physical routers in a network.
It uses data labels rather than network addresses
It is commonly used with technologies such as MPLS, 4G, and 5G

It also allows networks to route traffic based on application needs rather than static routing tables or physical topologies.

MPLS uses data labels rather than network addresses.

SD- WAN operates at Layer 3 and above of the OSI model.

SD- WAN still uses routers; it just overlays them with software-defined controls.

Generally, symmetric encryption is faster than asymmetric encryption. 

Symmetric encryption does not inherently provide authentication, integrity, or non-repudiation.

Symmetric encryption is designed for encrypting text and decrypting ciphertext with the same key.

questions.stem:
What are the main components of the Sigma ecosystem?

Choose THREE.
questions.explanation:
Sigma is a standardized rule format used to describe SIEM detection logic. It is commonly used around Security Operations Centers (SOCs), threat hunting teams, and generally around the cyber security landscape. The Sigma format refers to the core of Sigma, which is YAML-based and used to define detection rules in a SIEM-independent way. Sigma tools are supporting utilities that assist with processing, validating, and converting Sigma rules, such as sigmac (the Sigma rule converter). Sigma rule collections are public or private repositories of ready-made Sigma rules, like those available from the official Sigma GitHub.

Sigma is not a threat intelligence feed, and it is not a tool for sandboxing.

Choose TWO.

options.text: Setting up firewalls that do ingress and egress filtering
Validating input on a web application's form fields

Setting up firewalls that do ingress and egress filtering can block malicious traffic at the network perimeter. questions.stem:
Which of the following are classified as voluntary frameworks?

Choose TWO.
questions.explanation:
Voluntary frameworks are available for organziations to implement on their own without being legally required to do so. questions.stem:
An internet service provider finds that traffic meant for one of its customers is being sent to an unknown network. That network has started announcing the customer's Internet Protocol (IP) prefix through Border Gateway Protocol (BGP).

Which mechanism helps prevent this type of route hijacking?

options.text: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) with MD5 authentication

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI)

Misconfigured or compromised Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routes have been exploited to reroute traffic through malicious networks. Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) lets network operators digitally sign route announcements and associate them with the legitimate holder of an Internet Protocol (IP) address block. Other networks can validate announced routes against these certificates and filter out invalid routes, preventing route hijacking and route leaks.

Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) adds digital signatures to Domain Name System (DNS) responses so resolvers can verify them. It does not stop a network from announcing BGP routes for IP prefixes it does not hold.

OSPF with MD5 authentication protects routing updates within an organization's internal network. It does not validate which networks are authorized to announce IP prefixes through BGP.

Transaction Signature (TSIG) authenticates and secures DNS zone transfers. It does not prevent BGP route hijacking.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are tactics that adversaries use?

Choose THREE.

options.text: Setting up a server for a command and control operation

questions.explanation:
Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) indicate the presence of an unauthorized entity trying to perform a blocked activity. Tactics are high-level goals, techniques are how those goals are achieved, and procedures are sequences of actions to execute an attack tactic. 

Reconnaissance is a tactic that involves gathering information to plan a future attack. Action on objectives is a tactic often used as a general label for achieving the final goal, such as data theft or system damage. Persistence is a tactic representing the goal of maintaining access over time, even after reboots.

Establishing a command and control center is a procedure that involves setting up architecture and corresponds to the tactic of command and control.

DLL injection is a technique, not a tactic, that is typically used for tactics such as defense evasion or privilege escalation.

questions.stem: The two most common algorithm types for encryption are asymmetric and symmetric. Of the following, which is NOT an asymmetric algorithm?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Blowfish

Blowfish is a symmetric algorithm. Asymmetric algorithms are much harder to decipher, but they require more complicated encryption methods that can take longer in certain instances. Asymmetric uses a public key to encrypt data so that only the private key can decrypt it. Rivest–Shamir–Adleman (RSA), Diffie-Hellman, and Elliptic-Curve Cryptography (ECC)  are all asymmetric encryption algorithms. 

Diffie-Hellman is used in the key agreement process and creates an encrypted channel to transfer keys securely, but it does not provide any other features such as authentication or confidentiality.

RSA can provide key exchange, encryption, and digital signatures. It can use a 1,024- to 4,096-bit key.

ECC is an algorithm based on elliptic curves.

questions.stem:
Which of the following types of events can result in alert fatigue?

Choose TWO.

options.text: Alert rules that are too general
Firewalls that log too much data

questions.explanation:
Alert fatigue involves security personnel receiving too many alerts to care about each one, which can result in a real threat being missed. Too many false positives means that security analysts waste time chasing harmless events. Alert rules that are too general can generate excessive alerts.

False negatives are missed detections, so they would not cause alert fatigue because they do not generate alerts.

Firewalls that log too much data do not generate alerts by themselves unless the logs are incorrectly triggering alerts. 

Decrypting traffic is resource intensive, but it does not inherently cause alert fatigue.

Choose TWO.

Acme Inc. has thoroughly reviewed and analyzed risks and implemented the proper controls to mitigate them for a group of assets. However, a security engineer points out that there is still some risk the organization was unable to eliminate. 

What term describes the risk the security engineer is highlighting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Residual risk

Residual risk is leftover risk after controls and mitigations have been implemented. Residual risk represents the fact that you cannot eliminate all risk. 

Inherent risk is the risk that is a fundamental part of a given activity. For example, there is some inherent risk of getting caught in the rain if you go for a long walk. 

Risk deterrence involves actions, systems, and policies that discourage exploiting vulnerabilities or realizing risk.

A false positive occurs when a system incorrectly identifies legitimate activity as a threat.

questions.stem: Which term describes the concept of data being subject to the laws in which it resides or passes through?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Data sovereignty

Organizations need to be aware that they are responsible for where their data resides or passes through. Data sovereignty can inform decisions such as where to locate servers and which routes data should take as it travels to its destination.

Data ownership refers to who is ultimately responsible for data. 

Data compliance refers broadly to meeting regulatory requirements but not specifically for jurisdictional control. 

Data lakes are centralized repositories that store large amounts of raw data.

questions.stem:
A company's intrusion detection system (IDS) has learned that the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) mail server normally generates about 23% of network traffic. The IDS raises an alert when the mail server suddenly generates 70% of all traffic, even though no known attack signature matches.

Which detection technique generated the alert?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Anomaly-based detection

Anomaly-based detection learns what normal activity looks like, such as usual traffic volumes and routine user actions, and alerts when observed events depart significantly from that baseline. A Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server whose share of traffic jumps from 23% to 70% is exactly that kind of departure. Because it does not depend on signatures, this method can catch threats that have never been seen before.

Signature-based detection compares events against a database of known attack signatures written by the vendor or operator. It is limited to known patterns, so it would not alert on traffic that matches no signature.

Behavior-based detection, also called heuristic-based detection, uses predefined rules to flag actions that match known patterns of malicious activity. An example is repeated failed logins followed by a successful login, which could indicate a brute-force attack.

Stateful inspection is a firewall capability that tracks the state of active connections, such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) sessions. It is used to allow or block traffic based on connection state rather than to detect deviations from a traffic baseline.

questions.stem: After a cyber espionage attack, analysts discover that the malware's code stylometry, reused command-and-control infrastructure, and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) match those previously documented for an advanced persistent threat (APT) group. Which malware analysis outcome BEST describes linking the attack to this group?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Malware attribution

Malware attribution ties malware or an attack to a particular threat group, adversary, or nation-state using evidence such as distinctive code signatures, stylometry, reused infrastructure, or operating methods. Espionage malware can be linked to an advanced persistent threat (APT) group when its coding style, infrastructure, and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) match what has been documented about that group. Intezer Analyze and Maltego are tools that support attribution.

Variant matching determines whether a sample is a variant of a known malware family. It links samples to a family rather than linking an attack to a specific threat actor.

Indicator of compromise (IoC) extraction collects details such as Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, hashes, and domains from a file for detection and sharing. It does not by itself identify the responsible group.

Code similarity analysis gauges how much two malware samples have in common in their code. It connects samples to one another but does not on its own tie an attack to a particular group.

questions.stem:
Which of the following scenarios should implement encryption for regulatory reasons in the U.S.?

Choose TWO.

options.text: An investment firm keeps records of clients' non-public financial histories
A social media platform stores users' ad preferences
A gaming company logs leaderboard scores for competitive players
A medical center stores patient health data in the cloud
A merchant keeps contact information of past customers

questions.explanation:
U.S. data privacy and security regulations often require strong security safeguards, and encryption is one way to meet these requirements. Protected Health Information (PHI) falls under HIPAA, which requires appropriate safeguards such as encryption, especially when data is transmitted or stored in the cloud. Non-public personal financial information is regulated under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), which recommends encryption to protect against unauthorized disclosure.

Ad preferences are not generally considered sensitive personal information.

Basic contact information like names and email addresses usually do not trigger mandatory encryption unless combined with more sensitive data such as SSNs or credit card numbers.

Gaming data would not be considered sensitive information to regulators.

Which of the following activities would an attacker use when pivoting?

Choose TWO.

options.text: Setting up sandboxes to run code
Using Netcat to communicate with other machines
Footprinting the system they are on
Modifying scheduled tasks to elevate access
Creating an SSH tunnel to forward traffic

Modifying scheduled tasks is used to attempt privilege escalation.

Setting up sandboxes is used to safely analyze code.

questions.stem:
An online ticketing company keeps its staging and production servers in the cloud. They want to be sure that if there is a vulnerability in a staging server, an attacker still won't have access to the production environment. 

Which solution can they implement to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Microsegmentation

Microsegmentation is a network security technique that involves dividing a cloud or data center environment into logically separated segments at a granular level, often down to the individual workload or application. In this scenario, the ticketing company wants to isolate staging and production servers, and microsegmentation ensures that even if one segment is compromised, lateral movement to the other environment would be blocked. 

Container security focuses on securing individual containers, so it wouldn’t directly solve the issue of isolating cloud environments, which might use virtual machines or other architectures beyond containers.

A Virtual Private Network (VPN) encrypts data and secures communication channels between endpoints but does not provide isolation.

Network Address Translation (NAT) hides internal IP addresses and can control outbound traffic, but it is not designed for environment isolation.

questions.stem: Which type of attack exploits the trust that a web application has in a logged-in user by tricking them into executing unauthorized actions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: CSRF

A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that exploits the trust a web application places in an authenticated user. The attacker tricks the user into unknowingly submitting a request to the web application, which then executes an action using the user’s authenticated session, such as changing passwords or transferring funds.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into content; however, XSS is about code injection rather than tricking authenticated users into sending requests. 

A confused deputy involves a legitimate system being tricked into misusing its authority by a less-privileged user. 

Time-Of-Check to Time-Of-Use (TOCTOU) is a race condition vulnerability, where an attacker exploits the gap between checking a resource and using it.

Supply chain risk management relates to risks from third-party vendors during procurement and delivery.

questions.stem:
Which of the following scenarios are examples of self-healing hardware?

Choose TWO.

options.text: A system automatically reverts to a known-good state after a problematic update
A laptop turns itself off to avoid overheating
An administrator performs a BIOS update during scheduled maintenance
A server with two PSUs automatically operates normally when one PSU fails
A file server implements disk striping with RAID

questions.explanation:
Self-healing hardware refers to systems designed to detect faults and automatically recover or maintain functionality without manual intervention. A redundant Power Supply Unit (PSU) ensures the system continues functioning even when one fails. A system automatically reverting to a known-good state after a problematic update can also be viewed as self-healing hardware even though it may relate more to software. 

Disk striping, or RAID 0, increases performance but offers no fault tolerance.

A laptop turning itself off to avoid overheating is damage prevention, not recovery.

An administrator performing a BIOS update during scheduled maintenance is a planned maintenance task.

questions.stem:
Which of the following scenarios are model inversions?

Choose TWO.

options.text: An attacker queries a facial recognition AI with inputs that help reconstruct identifiable facial features of a user
A malicious actor floods an LLM with numerous difficult questions
A user interacts with a medical AI model and finds out that a specific patient’s data was used to train it, violating privacy protections
An adversary mislabels training data so that the model learns the wrong information
A developer embeds API keys in source code accidentally uploaded to a public code repository

questions.explanation:
Model inversion attacks involve querying an AI model to reconstruct identifiable input data that the model was trained on. Querying a facial recognition AI with input that helps reconstruct identifiable facial features of a user is an inversion technique that can violate user privacy. Extracting training data about individual medical records from a model by interacting with it is also an example of model inversion because it forces the model to divulge its internal information.

Flooding an LLM with numerous difficult questions is a Denial of Service (DoS) attack.

Mislabeling training data is a training data poisoning attack.

Embedding API keys in source code accidentally uploaded to a public code repository is an issue related to secure coding practices.

questions.stem: A law firm must ensure that confidential emails can be read only by the intended recipients, even if the messages are stored on intermediate mail servers or a server is compromised. Which solution BEST meets this requirement?

options.text: Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption between mail servers

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) end-to-end encryption

Strong email security combines encryption, authentication protocols, and user awareness. End-to-end encryption (E2EE) with Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) or Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) means only the intended recipient can decrypt a message. The content stays protected on every server it passes through.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) encrypts emails in transit between systems, preventing interception on the network. Messages are not protected by TLS once they are stored on a mail server.

Sender Policy Framework (SPF) verifies that the sending server is authorized for the domain. It helps prevent spoofing but does not encrypt message content.

DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses signatures to verify that a message came from the claimed domain and was not altered. It does not prevent others from reading the message.

questions.stem:
A cloud data center team needs firewalls to enforce microsegmentation between workloads running on the same virtualization hosts. The firewalls' performance will depend on the computing resources the hypervisor allocates to them.

Which type of firewall fits this deployment?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Virtual firewall

A virtual firewall runs as an appliance on a virtual host managed by a hypervisor, so its performance depends on the computing resources the hypervisor gives it. Virtual firewalls are typically used in data centers and to enforce microsegmentation.

Hardware firewalls are dedicated appliances with their own central processing unit (CPU) and memory, which gives them very high performance. They are used for enterprise deployments rather than running as virtual workloads on a hypervisor.

Software firewalls run on a host operating system, such as Windows Defender Firewall or Linux iptables, and share computing resources with that operating system. They are used to add security and defense in depth on individual hosts.

A web application firewall (WAF) inspects Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) and Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) traffic to protect web applications. It is not designed to enforce microsegmentation between virtual workloads.

questions.stem: A network security engineer is troubleshooting an IEEE 802.1X wireless authentication deployment using Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) with a RADIUS authentication server. Arrange the EAP authentication activities in the correct sequence.

options.text: The authenticator enforces the authorization decision by granting appropriate network access, applying segmentation controls, and logging the authentication session for monitoring and auditing.
The authenticator requests the client's identity and forwards the EAP exchange between the client and the RADIUS server.
The client device connects, and the authenticator blocks general network access until authentication is completed.
The authentication server returns an authentication success or failure decision along with authorization attributes such as VLAN assignment, access restrictions, and network policies.
The authentication server validates client credentials, certificates, or MFA requirements using the configured EAP method and identity provider integrations.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

The client device connects, and the authenticator blocks general network access until authentication is completed: The authenticator places the port in an unauthorized state from the moment a device connects until the full EAP exchange completes.
The authenticator requests the client's identity and forwards the EAP exchange between the client and the RADIUS server: The authenticator relays the EAP conversation between the supplicant and the authentication server.
The authentication server validates client credentials, certificates, or MFA requirements using the configured EAP method and identity provider integrations: With the identity forwarded, the RADIUS server performs the actual cryptographic and credential validation according to its configured EAP method.

questions.stem:
What are some techniques to reduce the risk of a user achieving privilege escalation?

Choose THREE.

options.text: Confirming that full-disk encryption has been properly configured
Making sure that databases do not run as the root or as an administrative user
Ensuring that applications are operating with the minimum permissions needed to run
Verifying that users are given the minimum amount of permissions needed to perform their jobs
Checking that the system is running a host-based firewall

questions.explanation:
Privilege escalation attacks allow an attacker to go from a basic account to a higher-level account on a system, giving them more options for attacks. 

Ensuring that applications are operating with the minimum permissions needed to run aligns with the principle of least privilege, which reduces the attack surface by limiting what an application can do, even if it is compromised. Likewise, verifying that users are given the minimum amount of permissions needed to perform their jobs also supports the principle of least privilege. Databases should run with non-privileged service accounts to reduce the risk of full system compromise if the database is exploited.

A host-based firewall is a good general practice, but it does not directly mitigate privilege escalation.

Full disk encryption can protect data at rest but is not related to restricting privilege levels.

questions.stem:
Which of the following accurately describe JTAG?

Choose TWO.

options.text: It is a method to prevent VLAN hopping
It is used to extract data from a chip
It involves soldering wires onto metal taps on a circuit board
It automatically encrypts data found during digital forensics
It is designed to create an isolated computing environment

questions.explanation:
Joint Test Action Group (JTAG), named after the organization that standardized it, involves hardware-level security assessments and chip-level data extraction. A common method involves a physical connection to test pads or pins on a circuit board, which may involve soldering wires to specific points. JTAG interfaces can be used to read memory, debug firmware, or access internal registers.

Sandboxing or virtualization is designed to create an isolated computing environment.

JTAG does not have built-in encryption capabilities.

VLAN hopping is a network attack technique, and JTAG is unrelated to network security.

questions.stem:
What are some solutions that aim to achieve interoperability between systems?

Choose THREE.
questions.explanation:
Interoperability refers to systems, applications, and services that can work together and share data or authenticate across different environments. Single Sign-On (SSO) is an interoperability solution because it allows users to authenticate once and gain access to multiple systems. The Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) is an open standard used to exchange authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers. OAuth is an authorization framework that enables users to grant access to their data across different applications without sharing login credentials.

A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a security solution that filters and monitors traffic to and from a web application but does not enable interoperability between systems.

Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) aggregates and normalizes security data from multiple sources but does enable interoperability between systems.

Zero trust architecture is a security model that assumes no inherent trust in any other system, so it does not focus on making systems work together.

questions.stem: A financial institution needs a way to securely generate cryptographic keys. What type of device can they use for this?

A Self-Encrypting Drive (SED) is a drive that has built-in encryption and decryption. 

An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is a device that looks for malicious activity. 

A Security Information and Event Manager (SIEM) collects and analyzes log files for malicious activity.

Caching is used to store frequently accessed information.

questions.stem: An organization creates a document that lists what employees must do after a security breach, such as isolating affected systems from the network and alerting the security team right away. What type of security program documentation is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Procedure

A procedure explains how to carry out a policy. Policies state what must be done; procedures give the specific steps for doing it. A document listing the actions employees take after a breach, such as isolating affected systems and alerting the security team, is an incident response procedure.

A guideline helps interpret a policy by offering recommendations rather than required steps. Password creation guidelines that suggest character mixes are a typical example.

A standard is a benchmark that helps organizations measure and align their security practices. International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC) 27001, which provides a framework for an information security management system (ISMS), is one example.

A policy is a formal document that establishes what is required, such as mandating multifactor authentication (MFA) for critical systems. It sets the requirement but does not list the operational steps for carrying it out.

questions.stem:
A cloud service provider that stores customer data wants an independent evaluation of its controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. Its customers specifically ask for a report based on the Trust Services criteria established by the American Institute of CPAs (AICPA).

What should the provider obtain?

options.text: A Service Organization Control Type 2 (SOC 2) audit
A Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM) gap review
A National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) self-assessment
A Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks assessment

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A Service Organization Control Type 2 (SOC 2) audit

A Service Organization Control Type 2 (SOC 2) audit, based on standards from the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA), examines an organization's controls over security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. Its reports follow the AICPA Trust Services criteria, which makes it especially useful for providers that hold customer data in the cloud.

A Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks assessment compares system configurations against consensus-driven hardening guidelines. It measures configuration baselines rather than producing a report on the Trust Services criteria.

A National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) self-assessment helps an organization assess and prioritize cybersecurity risk across five core functions. It is voluntary and internally driven, so it does not provide an independent report on the Trust Services criteria.

A Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) Cloud Controls Matrix (CCM) gap review compares cloud controls against CSA control objectives. It supports cloud security best practices but is not the AICPA report customers requested.

questions.stem:
What are some benefits to using DMARC?

Choose TWO.

options.text: DMARC prevents email spoofing by modifying the sender’s address
DMARC provides feedback to domain owners through reports
DMARC allows domain owners to specify how receiving mail servers should handle unauthenticated emails
DMARC authenticates email attachments using digital signatures
DMARC uses public-key cryptography, where the sender signs emails with a private key and recipients verify the signature using a public key stored in DNS

questions.explanation:
Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance (DMARC) works with SPF and DKIM to handle issues related to email. DMARC allows domain owners to specify how receiving mail servers should handle unauthenticated emails, such as doing nothing, rejecting them, or quarantining them. DMARC generates aggregate and forensic reports that help domain owners see how their domain is being used.

DKIM is the technology that uses public-key cryptography, where the sender signs emails with a private key and recipients verify the signature using a public key stored in DNS.

DMARC only authenticates the headers and sender information, not the attachment.

DMARC does not modify the sender’s address; it sets policies on handling spoofed email.

questions.stem:
Which of the following scenarios demonstrate residual risk?

Choose TWO.

options.text: A logistics company determines that it is too risky to hold onto customer payment information, so they hand this task over to a third party
A hospital has implemented a strict access control system to systems that temporarily hold patient data during medical procedures, but a user with legitimate credentials misuses the system
A water park does a vulnerability assessment and decides that the risk of fire is too low, so they do not create any controls to address this risk
A manufacturer conducts regular security audits on their suppliers, but one supplier suffers a data breach that affects the manufacturer's production
A financial institution decides that they will not build an app because it is possible that a security flaw in their code could put user funds at risk

questions.explanation:
Residual risk refers to the risk that remains after all security controls and mitigation strategies have been applied. A user with legitimate credentials misusing the system is an example a risk that remains even though controls have been applied. Similarly, a supplier suffering a data breach that affects the manufacturer's production is a risk that remains despite regular security audits.

Determining that it is too risky to do something and then handing this task over to a third party is an example of risk transference.

Deciding that a risk is too low and not doing anything to control it is an example of risk acceptance.

Deciding to not build an app because it is possible that a security flaw in their code could put user funds at risk is an example of risk avoidance.

questions.stem: An organization needs an open-source encryption system to enable the signing and encryption of email messages using keys the organization themselves manages. Which of the following meets their requirements?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: GPG

GNU Privacy Guard (GPG) is an open-source encryption system closely related to Pretty Good Privacy (PGP). Both programs were developed to protect electronic communications and enable digital signing and encryption. GPG is a rewrite or upgrade of PGP. It is considered more secure than PGP. Sending secure emails is a common use for GPG. 

Secure SHell (SSH) is a network protocol for securely connecting to remote computers.

Digital Rights Management (DRM) is used to protect digital intellectual property from unauthorized use.

Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is an option for creating secure connections to servers. It interfaces with the application and transport layers but does not really operate within these layers.

ISO/IEC 27001 is a framework that focuses on internal auditing. It covers 14 domains in total.

questions.stem: A company wants to protect www.example.com and shop.example.net, two completely different domain names, using a single certificate. Which type of certificate should the company request?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Subject alternative name (SAN) certificate

A subject alternative name (SAN) certificate covers several domain names or Internet Protocol (IP) addresses with one certificate. A wildcard certificate covers only subdomains of a single domain, but a SAN certificate can include entirely unrelated domains. One SAN certificate could protect both www.example.com and shop.example.net.

A wildcard certificate secures multiple subdomains of a single domain, such as *.example.com. It cannot cover a different domain such as example.net.

An extended validation (EV) certificate provides the highest level of identity verification through extensive checks by the certificate authority. The validation level does not determine how many different domains a certificate covers.

An organization validation (OV) certificate verifies domain ownership and some organizational information. It provides more trust than a domain validation certificate but does not by itself cover multiple different domains.

questions.stem: Different encryption methods use different techniques to enhance security. Of the following, which technique involves running data through a cryptographic function to provide a one-way verification of data integrity?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Hashing

When data is being hashed, it is run through an algorithm to produce a one-way message digest that allows a user to verify that the data is original and unaltered. Hashes provide a fixed-length string after hashing, no matter what data is fed into the algorithm. If the data that was hashed is changed in any way, it will provide a completely different hash than the previous one.

Symmetric encryption is a type of two-way cryptographic function because encrypted data is intended to be decrypted using a specific key. 

Code signing is a process in which a software creator cryptographically signs code or scripts to enable validation of the source. 

Steganography hides information but does not ensure integrity.

Sideloading is the process of installing an app from an unauthorized or unofficial source.

questions.stem:
A large organization is deploying a public key infrastructure (PKI) and needs to onboard users at many sites. It wants identity verification to be distributed so that a trusted intermediary confirms each requester's identity before certificates are issued.

Which PKI component performs this role?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Registration authority (RA)

A registration authority (RA) checks the identity of whoever requests a certificate. In a public key infrastructure (PKI), the RA acts as a trusted go-between, completing identity checks before the certificate authority (CA) issues the certificate. An RA is optional but common in large or distributed deployments, such as onboarding users at many sites.

The root certificate authority (CA) sits at the top of the PKI trust hierarchy. Intermediate or issuing CAs typically handle signing certificate requests, and identity verification can be delegated to an RA.

The Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) provides real-time checks of whether a certificate is still valid. It is used to validate existing certificates rather than to verify requesters' identities.

A certificate revocation list (CRL) is published by a CA to identify certificates that are no longer valid. It supports revocation checking, not identity verification during enrollment.

questions.stem:
What are some reasons to use CIS as part of an organization's information security strategy?

Choose TWO.

options.text: To get real-time threat intelligence feeds for all industries
To discover best practices in security controls
To align security practices with industry-recognized frameworks like NIST and ISO/IEC 27001
To get automatic patches for vulnerable services
To automatically detect and mitigate zero-day vulnerabilities

questions.explanation:
The Center for Internet Security (CIS) is a non-profit group that publishes controls that are useful for contributing to an organization's information security strategy. The CIS controls offer best practices for securing IT systems and data and help organizations focus on high-impact activities to reduce risk. CIS controls can be mapped to widely adopted frameworks such as NIST CSF and ISO/IEC 27001, and that helps organizations meet compliance goals.

CIS does not provide patch management tools or automatic patching services.

While CIS offers some threat intelligence, real-time feeds for all industries are not its primary function.

CIS does not offer automated threat detection or zero-day mitigation tools.

questions.stem:
A company must protect a customer database at rest to meet General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements. The database administrators want encryption that secures the stored database files without requiring changes to the applications that use the database.

Which technology should they use?

options.text: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) over Transport Layer Security (TLS)

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)

Data at rest is data sitting in physical or cloud storage, such as a database. Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) encrypts database files at rest without changes to the applications that use them and helps meet regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Good practice also includes strong algorithms such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES-256), key management based on a hardware security module (HSM), and regular key rotation.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) protects data in transit, such as web traffic. It does not encrypt the database files stored on disk.

Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) protects data in transit, such as virtual private network (VPN) connections. It does not secure stored database files.

Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) over TLS creates an encrypted channel for email transmission. It protects messages in transit rather than databases at rest.

Which type of certificate is stored on the card?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Smart card certificate

A smart card certificate authenticates a user through a physical card whose chip holds the user's private key. These certificates are common in high-security settings, such as government agencies and secure corporate sites. Using the card to sign in to the network and sensitive applications gives the employee strong two-factor authentication.

Code signing certificates digitally authenticate software or applications. They verify the source and integrity of code rather than authenticating users to a network.

Domain validation (DV) certificates provide basic encryption for websites after the certificate authority verifies domain ownership. They are not used for user authentication.

Wildcard certificates secure multiple subdomains of a domain using a single certificate, such as *.example.com. They protect websites rather than authenticating individual users.

questions.stem: A high-traffic public website needs a component in front of its web servers that manages inbound requests, caches static content, distributes traffic across multiple servers, and offloads Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption and decryption from the back end. Which component should be deployed?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Reverse proxy

A reverse proxy sits in front of internal servers and handles the requests coming in to them, which is why busy websites rely on it. It can cache static content to lighten the load on application servers, add a layer of security, and spread incoming traffic across servers for high availability. It can also take over Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encryption and decryption from the back end; HAProxy and Squid are common examples.

A forward proxy controls outbound traffic from internal clients to the internet. It filters and caches content for users rather than managing inbound requests to web servers.

An application programming interface (API) gateway manages and secures API traffic, such as validating tokens and enforcing rate limits. It is not primarily used to cache static content and offload encryption for web servers.

A web application firewall (WAF) inspects Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) and Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) traffic for attacks such as Structured Query Language (SQL) injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). It filters malicious requests but does not cache content or distribute traffic across servers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a data subject's right under GDPR?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The right to object

A data subject can object to the processing of their personal data. This is useful for users who want to stop their data from being used for marketing or profiling purposes. 

Other data subject's rights under GDPR include the following: 

Rights related to automatic profiling and decisions
The right to be informed
The right to access data
The right to rectification
The right to data portability
The right to erasure
The right to restrict processing

The other answer choices are not data subjects' rights under GDPR.

questions.stem: What authentication protocol involves the server sending a random string to request authentication and the client encrypting that string with a password?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: CHAP

Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol (CHAP) involves the server sending a random string to request authentication and the client encrypting that string with a password. The client then sends the encrypted string back to the server. If the server can decrypt the string successfully with the password, authentication is successful. 

Password Authentication Protocol (PAP) provides authentication but is insecure because it transmits credentials in cleartext.

Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for port-based access control.

Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol (PEAP) encapsulates the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) within a secure private tunnel.

questions.stem: Acme, Inc. had sensitive data stolen because they purchased a malware-infected server from an IT vendor. What type of attack did Acme, Inc. fall victim to?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Supply chain attack

Supply chain attacks occur when a threat actor compromises an organization by first compromising a part of the organization's supply chain such as a vendor or delivery service.

Denial of Service (DoS) attacks occur when a threat actor prevents legitimate access to a service.

Credential stuffing attacks use stolen or leaked credentials from one organization to gain unauthorized access to another system.

A baiting attack can involve dropping infected USB sticks or other storage media near victims.

questions.stem: The CISO at Acme Hospital wrote a policy on securely storing patient data to comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 ( HIPAA). What type of policy did the CISO write?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Regulatory 

A regulatory policy is a policy based on a law or regulatory standards. A policy based on HIPAA regulations is an example of a regulatory policy. Regulatory polices help align organizational practices with the laws and standards they must comply with. 

Advisory policies explain the consequences of not performing certain actions or not following specific guidelines. An Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) is a textbook example of an advisory policy. 

Informative policies help the target understand a specific policy. The key difference between an advisory policy and an informative policy is that an informative policy is not enforced. A retail store's return policy is an example of an informative policy.

Polymorphic is a type of virus behavior, not a type of policy.

Which of the following accurately describe IEEE 802.1X?

It is composed of a supplicant, authenticator, and authentication server

questions.stem: A company finds that dozens of unmanaged personal phones and tablets are accessing corporate data without any security controls in place. Which solution BEST addresses this issue?

options.text: Enforce device policies through mobile device management (MDM)
Require multifactor authentication for all corporate applications
Configure time-based access control for all users
Apply geographic restrictions to corporate data access

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Enforce device policies through mobile device management (MDM)

As mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) devices multiply, organizations face device sprawl: more unmanaged devices connecting to the network than they can control. An employee's personal phone reaching corporate data with no security controls is a typical case. Device access policies enforced through mobile device management (MDM) ensure that only approved, secure devices can connect, and network segmentation limits what sensitive resources are exposed.

Multifactor authentication strengthens verification of the user's identity. Authenticated users could still access corporate data from unmanaged devices with no security controls.

Time-based access control limits the hours when users can reach resources. Unmanaged devices could still reach data during allowed hours.

Geographic restrictions limit access based on location. Unmanaged devices inside permitted locations could still reach corporate data.

Device access policies enforced through mobile device management (MDM) ensure that only approved, secure devices can connect, and network segmentation limits what sensitive resources are exposed.

Multifactor authentication strengthens verification of the user's identity. Authenticated users could still access corporate data from unmanaged devices with no security controls.

Time-based access control limits the hours when users can reach resources. Unmanaged devices could still reach data during allowed hours.

Geographic restrictions limit access based on location. Unmanaged devices inside permitted locations could still reach corporate data.

questions.stem:
Which of the following accurately describe a software bill of materials?

Choose TWO.

options.text: It is enforced by a regulation in the U.S. that requires all publicly available software to list its libraries and dependencies
It automates patch deployment for third-party software dependencies
It is a nested inventory of components that make up a piece of software
It works with the Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX) to attest if a product is affected by a known vulnerability

questions.explanation:
A Software Bill Of Materials (SBOMs) is a structured inventory detailing all components, libraries, and dependencies within a piece of software. SBOMs provide visibility into software components, including third-party libraries, open-source dependencies, and proprietary code. SBOMs can be used alongside VEX documents, which indicate whether specific vulnerabilities impact a product, helping organizations prioritize remediation effort.

Executive Order 14028 has promoted SBOM, but there is no universal regulation requiring all publicly available software to disclose its components.

An SBOM is a documentation tool, not a patching solution. 

SBOMs support software transparency and security, not privacy regulation compliance such as GDPR.

questions.stem:
What are some examples of attacks on embedded systems?

Choose THREE.

options.text: An insulin pump broadcasts unencrypted health telemetry over Bluetooth
Firmware on a webcam has a vulnerability that lets anyone with camera's public IP address view live footage
A cloud database exposes its admin panel due to misconfigured IAM roles
A developer fails to sanitize SQL input in a CRM platform
A file server allows unencrypted Telnet connections for remote management
A car's wireless entry system has a default code that allows anyone to reprogram the keys

questions.explanation:
Embedded systems are computing devices integrated into hardware like webcams, cars, routers, and medical devices. These systems often have unique attack surfaces due to limited interfaces, outdated firmware, or weak security configurations. Firmware on a webcam that has a vulnerability that lets anyone with camera's public IP address view live footage is a serious issue with an embedded system. Vehicles have many embedded systems, including keyless entry that could be exploited if it is vulnerable. An insulin pump broadcasting unencrypted health telemetry over Bluetooth could allow an attacker to interfere with critical health functions.

A file server allowing unencrypted Telnet connections for remote management is an example of a misconfiguration and is not considered an embedded system.

A developer failing to sanitize SQL input in a CRM platform is a SQL injection vulnerability.

A cloud database exposes its admin panel due to misconfigured IAM roles is a cloud misconfiguration.

When there is an incident, the most volatile information should be collected first, so that it does not get overwritten. The most volatile information is the CPU, cache, and registers.

Kernel statistics is in the list of the second-most volatile components. 

Memory is the third-most volatile component. 

Swap space is the fourth most volatile component.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are steps involved in manual patch management?

Choose TWO.

options.text: Verifying the patches after they have been installed
Checking if patches are not critical, so they can be skipped
Testing the patches before deploying them

questions.explanation:
Manual patch management involves systematically updating software, firmware, or systems without automated tools. Proper testing in a controlled environment ensures that patches do not introduce unintended issues such as software conflicts or performance degradation. After deployment, verification ensures that patches were successfully applied and did not disrupt functionality.

Patch rollback is not a standard step in manual patch management.

Disabling antivirus software is not recommended, as it exposes the system to threats during patching.

Skipping patches arbitrarily can leave vulnerabilities unpatched.

questions.stem:
An organization tests its disaster recovery plan by assuming key systems are offline after a data center fire. The information technology (IT) team switches over to the backup data center in a sandbox environment, initiates mock failover protocols, and measures its response against the predefined recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO). Production systems are not disrupted.

Which type of test is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Simulation of a disaster scenario

A disaster scenario simulation tests a business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) plan by modeling the effects of a specific disaster in a controlled setting. It goes beyond discussion with hands-on steps, such as failing over to a backup data center on paper or in a sandbox. The team's performance is measured against the recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) without putting production systems at risk.

A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based session in which participants talk through their roles and actions. It does not involve hands-on activities such as mock failover.

A full-scale operational test is a live, end-to-end exercise that actually shuts down systems and fails production workloads over to a secondary site. It disrupts real operations, unlike this test.

An incident response walkthrough is a structured exercise used to verify incident response plans for protecting sensitive data. It reviews response steps rather than performing mock failover of disaster recovery systems.

questions.stem:
A security operations center (SOC) uses Splunk today but plans to move to another security information and event management (SIEM). It wants to write detection logic for suspicious PowerShell use and privilege escalation once, in YAML, and convert the rules into queries for whichever SIEM it uses.

Which rule-based language should it use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Sigma

Sigma is an open, rule-based standard for writing log detection rules that are not tied to any one security information and event management (SIEM) product. Rules are written in YAML and state which log entries to look for, and converters translate them into queries for platforms such as Splunk or Elastic. Sigma is often compared to Snort for logs, and the same rule can detect MITRE ATT&CK techniques on different SIEMs.

YARA uses rules to match string or binary patterns in files or memory and is used mainly for malware classification and file analysis. It does not define SIEM log queries.

Snort is a real-time network intrusion detection system/ intrusion prevention system (IDS/IPS) that uses rules to inspect packets for known attack patterns. It analyzes network traffic, not SIEM log data.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are accurate regarding automated patching?

Choose THREE.

options.text: Patch testing in a staging environment is recommended before enabling automated patch deployment in production
Automated patching requires extensive knowledge of object-oriented programming
Patches done through WSUS do not need testing, as they have passed Microsoft's quality assurance programs
Group Policy is used with WSUS for configuration settings
WSUS is an automated patch management solution for Windows

questions.explanation:
Automated patch management is an essential function for keeping systems patched in a timely manner before a new vulnerability can be exploited. Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) allows organizations to centrally manage and automate the distribution of updates and patches to Windows computers. Group Policy Objects (GPOs) are used to configure client settings for WSUS, such as specifying the update server, scheduling automatic updates, and managing update behavior. Testing patches helps avoid issues caused by faulty update.

Automated patching typically does not require programming knowledge, although some scripting knowledge can be helpful. 

While Microsoft tests updates, compatibility issues can still arise, making additional testing a good best practice before full deployment.

questions.stem:
Before a formal compliance review, a company hires an independent third party to evaluate its network and application security. The goal is to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and gaps that will guide future security improvements.

Which type of evaluation is this?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: External assessment

An assessment evaluates an organization's security posture to find vulnerabilities, risks, and gaps, usually to guide improvements or get ready for an audit. When an independent third party performs it, it is an external assessment and gives an objective view. External assessors can also bring expertise that helps the organization prepare for formal audits.

An external audit is a systematic, formal review that verifies compliance with established standards, regulations, or policies. Audits focus on adherence to specific requirements rather than on identifying areas for improvement.

A certification is a formal recognition granted after an organization meets specific standards. For organizations, it often involves passing an audit by an authorized certification body.

An internal audit is conducted by the organization's own audit or security team. It verifies compliance with internal policies and helps prepare for external audits.

questions.stem:
A former employee's certificate was revoked by the company's certificate authority (CA) two months ago and appears on the current certificate revocation list (CRL). However, logs show that a virtual private network (VPN) gateway accepted the certificate last week, allowing the former employee to reach a sensitive system.

What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: The CA never revoked the certificate
The certificate's validity period has expired
The certificate is a wildcard certificate
The gateway is not checking revocation status

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The gateway is not checking revocation status

A certificate is revoked when it should no longer be trusted, for example after the employee it was issued to leaves. Revocation protects only systems that look it up, so relying systems should check certificate status regularly through the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) or certificate revocation lists (CRLs). This certificate is on the CRL, yet the gateway accepted it, which means the gateway is not checking revocation.

An expired certificate would be rejected rather than accepted. Expiration also does not explain why a revoked certificate was trusted.

The certificate appears on the current CRL, which shows the certificate authority (CA) did revoke it. The failure is on the system relying on the certificate.

Wildcard certificates secure multiple subdomains of a domain with one certificate. The certificate type does not explain why a revoked certificate was accepted.

questions.stem:
Which activities need to occur in preparation for an incident?

Choose TWO.
questions.explanation:
The preparation phase of the incident response lifecycle includes proactive activities undertaken before a security incident occurs. Training ensures that personnel understand their roles and responsibilities for when an incident happens. Testing, such as tabletop exercises, simulations, and red teaming, help validate incident response plans before the actual event.

Analysis occurs during or after an incident to understand what happened and how it can be mitigated in the future.

Isolation refers to separating affected systems to prevent the spread of an incident and occurs during incident response, not preparation. 

Containment involves limiting the impact of an incident, such as halting malicious activity, and is part of the response phase.

questions.stem:
A healthcare analytics firm is adopting the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks to harden its servers. Because the servers support a high-security environment, the firm wants the most rigorous configuration controls and accepts that they may have greater operational impact.

Which option should the firm implement?

options.text: Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) benchmarks

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Level 2 benchmarks

The Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks come in two levels. Level 2 adds stricter controls intended for high-security environments, and those controls often affect operations more. A firm that wants the strongest hardening and accepts the usability tradeoff should choose Level 2.

Level 1 benchmarks provide baseline security settings chosen to keep the impact on usability low. They are a good starting point but are not the most rigorous option.

Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) benchmarks are a format of the CIS Benchmarks, available with a premium account, that can be used to scan a system automatically with the Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP). The format determines how a benchmark is consumed, not how rigorous its controls are.

CIS-CAT Pro is an automation tool that can be used to implement and assess the CIS Benchmarks. It applies whichever benchmark level is chosen rather than being a set of controls itself.

questions.stem:
Which of the following techniques are used in the field of malware attribution?

Choose TWO.
questions.explanation:
Malware attribution involves identifying the origin of a piece of malware. It helps organizations understand threat actors, anticipate future attacks, and take legal or strategic actions. Code stylometry analyzes programming styles to help attribute code to specific developers or groups. Variant matching detects similarities between malware strains, helping researchers link new malware to previously known families or actors, as attackers often reuse previous malware with modifications.

Detonation is used to observe malware behavior in a controlled environment to understand functionality but not attribution.

Encryption key length is a security parameter, not a method for identifying malware authorship.

CPU spikes can help detect malware but does not reveal the malware’s creator.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of symmetric encryption?

options.text: Easy key exchange on public networks

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Using a shared key

Symmetric encryption depends on both entities having a shared key that can decrypt the encrypted data. Because the key must be shared, it presents challenges when it needs to be exchanged on public networks. 

Easy key exchange is a characteristic of asymmetric encryption. 

Hash functions are generally one-way functions, where the input cannot be derived from the output, while with symmetric encryption, the input can be derived from the output if you have the shared key.

Using a public key is a characteristic of asymmetric encryption.

questions.stem:
An attacker attempts a brute-force login against a Linux server's Secure Shell (SSH) port, generating hundreds of identical failed-login events. The security information and event management ( SIEM) creates a separate alert for each event, overwhelming analysts.

Which configuration BEST addresses this?

options.text: Raising the SSH server's logging level to emergency only
Disabling the correlation rule for failed logins
Shortening the SIEM's log retention period for authentication logs
Deduplication with a threshold rule that aggregates events into one alert

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Deduplication with a threshold rule that aggregates events into one alert

Event duplication fills the security information and event management ( SIEM) system with repeated copies of the same event and slows it down. Deduplication normalizes the raw logs, applies a correlation or threshold rule, such as more than five failed attempts from one Internet Protocol (IP) address in a minute, and suppresses the repeats. Analysts then receive a single, high-fidelity alert describing the attack, which cuts alert fatigue and speeds triage.

Raising the logging level to emergency only would stop most failed-login events from being logged. This would create a blind spot rather than producing a useful summarized alert.

Shortening retention reduces how long logs are stored. It does not reduce the number of alerts generated in real time.

Disabling the correlation rule for failed logins would stop the attack from being detected. The goal is to reduce redundant alerts while still alerting on the brute-force activity.

questions.stem:
A database administrator is choosing an encryption approach for large files at rest. The administrator wants a symmetric cipher that operates on fixed-size data blocks, such as 128 bits, and pads smaller inputs.

Which type of cipher meets this description?

options.text: An asymmetric algorithm such as elliptic curve cryptography (ECC)
A block cipher such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)
A stream cipher such as ChaCha20

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A block cipher such as Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)

Block ciphers such as AES encrypt data in fixed-size chunks, such as 128 bits, and pad any input shorter than a block. In modes such as Counter (CTR) or Galois/Counter Mode (GCM), they provide strong protection and are well suited to large files, databases, and other data at rest. AES is specified in Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 197 and is the standard choice for file, full-disk, and database encryption.

Stream ciphers such as ChaCha20 process data one bit or byte at a time and need no padding. They fit real-time applications rather than fixed-size block processing.

A one-time pad provides unbreakable encryption when a truly random key at least as long as the message is used. It is effective for short messages but challenging to implement at scale.

Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is an asymmetric algorithm that uses public and private key pairs. It is not a symmetric cipher that processes fixed-size blocks.

questions.stem:
What are some steps that can be taken to secure BIOS and UEFI?

Choose TWO.
questions.explanation:
Securing BIOS and UEFI firmware is critical to ensuring the integrity of the boot process and preventing low-level attacks. Using open case alerts can let an administrator know if there has been a tampering attempt. Setting a BIOS/UEFI password is an extra layer of security.

Disabling virtualization does not inherently make BIOS/ UEFI more secure.

Legacy boot reduces security by bypassing Secure Boot and other protections.

Antivirus works at the OS level, not directly within firmware.

questions.stem: What should a well-designed hashing algorithm produce if provided with two different inputs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Two different outputs

Hashing algorithms are often used for data integrity and authentication. It is important for them to produce different outputs (hash values) given a different input. 

If two identical hash values are created from two different inputs, cybersecurity professionals call that a collision, which should be avoided.

Hashing algorithms do not combine multiple inputs into a single output.

Hash functions should not produce random output but rather deterministic output based on the input.

questions.stem:
Which of the following activities occur during an incident response?

Choose TWO.
questions.explanation:
Thee are specific activities that should occur during an incident response. One activity is root cause analysis, which helps responders understand the underlying cause of the incident, so it can be fully remediated and prevented in the future. Timeline reconstruction is also an important activity, which involves making a timeline of events to understand how an incident unfolded.

Dependency management refers to controlling software libraries during development or operations.

Browser isolation is a preventive control used to reduce the attack surface, often deployed to protect users from web-based threats. 

Continuous authorization refers to dynamic, real-time access decisions in a zero trust architecture.

questions.stem:
A company exposes microservices to partners through application programming interfaces (APIs). It needs a component that validates OAuth tokens and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), enforces rate limiting, blocks malformed requests, and hides backend service details from clients.

Which component should it implement?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: API gateway

An application programming interface (API) gateway sits between clients and backend services and routes each API request to the right place. It controls access using API keys, OAuth tokens, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), enforces rate limiting and throttling, and validates input to reject malformed or malicious requests. Many gateways also act as reverse proxies, routing requests while hiding backend details from clients.

A content delivery network (CDN) caches content on geographically distributed edge servers to reduce latency and absorb traffic. It does not validate API tokens or enforce per-client API policies.

A forward proxy controls outbound traffic from internal users to the internet. It is not designed to protect inbound API requests to backend services.

A network test access point (TAP) creates a physical copy of network traffic for monitoring. It does not enforce authentication or rate limits.

You have determined there is a 20% chance of compromise in the next year and that a compromise would lead to a loss of 50% of the value (half of the data) on the server.
